title: Chronological Log Merge Service for Cross-Region Correlation Reconciliation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We observe out-of-order and duplicate log records for multi-region requests where the correlation-id is shared across hops (edge->regional->core). This causes incorrect session reconstruction in the Console and inflated error-rate dashboards when events land in different ingestion regions or are replayed from backfills. Goal: implement a lightweight merge service that reorders and coalesces structured JSON envelopes across region boundaries based on correlated timestamps and a bounded reassembly window, emitting a single canonical event per logical operation into Loki/ELK sinks.
design_decision: We will keep the service stateless for scale: use Kafka topic partitions keyed by correlation-id (tenant-prefixed) and a compacting, time-bucketed in-memory merge window per partition. No global coordination; rely on monotonic event timestamps plus a configurable skew tolerance. If conflicting canonical fields exist, use deterministic precedence: (1) event with highest observed sequence_number, (2) if equal, event from source priority list (edge > regional > core). This trades off eventual correctness for predictable performance and low cross-region traffic.
architecture_notes: Components: (a) regional preprocessor sidecar that normalizes JSON envelope and stamps observed timestamp. (b) central Merge Service consumer group reading from cross-region merge topic. (c) small in-memory window keyed by (tenant, corr_id) with TTL and max-buffer-size. (d) output forwarder that writes the merged event to Loki and to an archival S3 cluster for audit.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary in us-west-2 on small tenant segment (~5% of traffic) with debug logging enabled. 2) Run in parallel: duplicate output to a 'merged-v2' Loki index while continuing legacy output to 'raw-v1' for 48h. 3) Compare matching counts, latency distribution, dashboard diffs; watch for reduced duplicate counts and corrected session lengths. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days if metrics stable. 5) Switch archival retention policy after 30 days.
acceptance_criteria: Merged event count equals unique correlation-id count within ±1% in canary tenants
No increase in end-to-end 99th percentile ingest latency by >20ms for canary partition
Duplicate events in Console session view reduced by >=90% for canary tenants
Automated regression alerts triggered for any increase in error-dashboard false positives
test_plan: Unit tests: window eviction, precedence rules, out-of-order buffering
Integration tests: synthetic cross-region traces replayed through sidecar -> kafka -> merge service -> loki-local
Chaos tests: inject dropped upstream messages and clock skew up to configured tolerance
Performance tests: sustained 10k corr_id/s at 1% skew with memory usage profiling
